evals.expected_output: A jobs_raw_{date}.json file written to output/ containing job listings from Greenhouse, Lever, and Built.in with all required schema fields populated and a run summary printed to stdout.

assertions.text: Output file is written to output/jobs_raw_{date}.json
Output JSON contains a top-level 'jobs' array with at least one entry
Every job has id, title, company, url, source, and posted_at fields
All jobs have is_remote: true or location containing 'remote'
No jobs have compensation.listed: true with max < 175000
Run summary is printed to stdout with counts per source

evals.prompt: Run the job scraper and look for staff and principal product manager openings at top tech companies. I want to make sure Stripe, Notion, and Anthropic are included.
evals.expected_output: JSON output with results from all three sources. Stripe, Notion, and Anthropic are queried via Greenhouse. Jobs are filtered to Staff PM / Principal PM titles. Any jobs with salary listed below $175k are excluded.

assertions.text: Output file is written to output/jobs_raw_{date}.json
sources.greenhouse.companies_queried includes stripe, notion, and anthropic tokens
All job titles match PM role keywords (product manager, staff, principal, senior, head of product)
No non-PM roles (engineer, designer, analyst) appear in the output

evals.prompt: What PM jobs are out there today? Check all your usual sources and give me a fresh list.
evals.expected_output: Full scrape run across all sources, deduplication applied, output written. The run summary shows counts from all three sources (Greenhouse, Lever, Built.in). No duplicate job URLs appear in the output.

assertions.text: Output file is written to output/jobs_raw_{date}.json
All three sources are represented in sources metadata (greenhouse, lever, builtin)
No duplicate URLs appear in the jobs array
scraped_at timestamp is present and in ISO 8601 format
